title: Classification of research publications based on data from OpenAlex
abstract: This data set contains an algorithmic classification of research publications based on data from OpenAlex. The classification is based on the OpenAlex snapshot from August 2025. To build the classification, we used the so-called extended direct citation approach in combination with the Leiden algorithm. The source code of our software is available here. The classification covers the 87 million journal articles and reviews, proceedings papers, preprints, and book chapters in OpenAlex that were published between 2000 and 2024 and that are connected to each other by citation links. Based on 2334 million citation links, we built a three-level hierarchical classification. Each publication was assigned to a cluster at each of the three levels of the classification. Clusters consist of publications that are relatively strongly connected by citation links and that can therefore be expected to be topically related. At each level of the classification, a publication was assigned to only one cluster, which means clusters do not overlap. The classification consists of 4521 micro clusters at the lowest (most granular) level, 917 meso clusters at the middle level, and 20 macro clusters at the highest (least granular) level. We also algorithmically linked each cluster in the classification to one or more of the following five broad main fields: biomedical and health sciences, life and earth sciences, mathematics and computer science, physical sciences and engineering, and social sciences and humanities. We used the Updated GPT 3.5 Turbo large language model, developed by OpenAI, to label the 4521 micro clusters at the lowest level in the classification. The source code of our software can be found here. See this blog post for more information about the classification. narrative:
Short impact summary

This dataset shows early practical uptake: Zenodo records 657 downloads and 5,934 views. The scholarly citation record is still empty in OpenAlex, so the evidence currently points to use and visibility rather than documented academic reuse.

Full narrative

Classification of research publications based on data from OpenAlex is a Zenodo-hosted dataset created by Nees Jan Van Eck at Leiden University. It presents an algorithmic classification of publications from the August 2025 OpenAlex snapshot, using an extended direct citation approach combined with the Leiden algorithm to organize a very large corpus of journal articles, reviews, proceedings papers, preprints, and book chapters.

The strongest signals in the record are usage-based. Zenodo reports 5,934 views and 657 downloads, which suggests that the dataset has attracted sustained attention from potential users. These numbers indicate that the resource is being discovered and accessed, even though the citation record has not yet accumulated.

At the same time, OpenAlex currently shows zero citations for the dataset, and scite records no citing or contrasting mentions. This is a quiet scholarly impact profile, but not a negative one; for a dataset of this kind, the record is simply still early or incomplete in terms of formal reuse evidence.

The stewardship signals are strong. Zenodo provides a persistent, open repository home with DOI-based identification, and OpenAIRE resolves multiple instances of the dataset, including open records. The presence of a related version in the repository metadata also indicates an ongoing versioned dataset lineage, which is important for reproducibility and long-term reuse.

Overall, the evidence points to a well-curated research dataset with clear technical relevance and visible use, especially through downloads and repository discovery. What can be said confidently from the record is that the dataset is available, findable, and being accessed; what cannot yet be claimed is documented scholarly citation impact.
